Notebook Cell Organizer can pass the collected Python imports through
[Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) before creating the import cell. This is
disabled by default, so installing Ruff is optional.

## Enable Ruff

Open VS Code Settings, search for `Notebook Cell Organizer`, and enable:

```json
{
  "notebook-cell-organizer.useRuffForImportSorting": true
}
```

The default command is equivalent to:

```bash
ruff check --select I --fix "${file}"
```

`${file}` is replaced with a temporary Python file containing only the imports
collected from the notebook.

## Use an absolute Ruff path

If Ruff is not available in the environment inherited by VS Code, configure
the executable directly:

```json
{
  "notebook-cell-organizer.useRuffForImportSorting": true,
  "notebook-cell-organizer.ruff.command": "/absolute/path/to/.venv/bin/ruff"
}
```

## Run Ruff through uv

The command and arguments are stored separately, so no shell is involved:

```json
{
  "notebook-cell-organizer.useRuffForImportSorting": true,
  "notebook-cell-organizer.ruff.command": "uv",
  "notebook-cell-organizer.ruff.arguments": [
    "run",
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--select",
    "I",
    "--fix",
    "${file}"
  ]
}
```

## Failure behavior

Ruff execution has a ten-second timeout. If the executable cannot be found,
the arguments do not contain `${file}`, Ruff reports an error, or the resulting
file is empty, the extension:

1. keeps the original collected imports;
2. completes the normal notebook organization;
3. writes the reason to the **Notebook Cell Organizer** output channel.

Ruff is only invoked for Python notebooks with at least one collected import.
